title: Incident Play Catalogue and Operator Skill Ladder
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary:

This document consolidates a curated catalogue of operational plays for common and high-risk incidents, paired with an explicit operator skill ladder and game-day curriculum. It is intended to be used by bridge operators, on-call engineers, SREs, and responder mentors to:
- Choose the correct play for an incident class,
- Run a consistent containment and restoration path, and
- Develop on-call competency through targeted exercises and measurable milestones.

Scope and purpose:
- Scope: Redwood production services, hosted inference clusters, dedicated capacity control plane, and customer-facing status communications.
- Purpose: reduce time-to-stabilize, lower variance in responder actions, preserve customer trust with clear messaging, and accelerate junior operator ramp.

When to consult this page:
1. Pager fires for production impacting alerts (P0/P1).
2. SLO burn rate > 5x sustained for 10m.
3. Multi-region degradation, cross-service cascading failures, or security-affecting incidents requiring coordinated comms.

Owner and escalation contacts:
- Primary owner: Eng SRE (sre@redwood.ai)
- Bridge lead rota: oncall-bridge@redwood.ai
- Escalation: Director of SRE (oncall escalation), Product Security for incidents with data/exposure implications.
- PagerDuty escalation policy: Redwood-Core-Routing -> SRE-Primary -> SRE-Secondary -> Eng-Director.

High-level incident classification (play selection):
- CLASS A (Critical): Service outage impacting >5% of customers or SLO loss > 25% in 15m. Use: Full-Bridge Orchestration (Play A).
- CLASS B (Degraded): Latency or error spikes affecting important routes or high-value customers. Use: Targeted Containment (Play B).
- CLASS C (Quality/regression): Model output quality regressions not causing availability loss. Use: Triage & Model Rollback (Play C).
- CLASS D (Security/PII): Suspected data leakage or auth bypass. Use: Isolate & Legal Notify (Play D).

Incident play catalogue (short reference):
Play A — Full-Bridge Orchestration (multi-region outage)
- Trigger: CLASS A detected OR multi-region 5xx rate > 3% for 10m.
- Immediate actions (first 5 minutes):
  1) Acknowledge pager and declare incident on status.redwood.ai (initial status: "Investigating").
  2) Create bridge (Zoom/Slack Huddle + PagerDuty bridge) and assign roles: Bridge Lead, System Experts (serving-runtime, routing), Comm Lead, Customer Liaison.
  3) Run quick blast: affect scope, estimated impact, first mitigation attempted.
- Diagnostics (5m–20m):
  - Check control-plane health: kubectl get pods -n redwood-control -o wide; check autoscaler logs.
  - Validate model-serving tiers: query /health endpoints for serving nodes; sample tail logs: sudo journalctl -u rwd-serving --since "10 minutes ago" | grep ERROR.
- Containment (20m–60m):
  - Activate cross-region fallback policy: route traffic to warm standby region per routing policy ID: route:fallback-ww-1.
  - If noisy neighbor suspected, apply per-pool admission control (scale down non-critical reservations).
- Restoration (60m+):
  - Gradually re-enable region with canary traffic (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) and monitor token latency P95 and error rate.
- Customer comms (timeline template in Appendix).

Play B — Targeted Containment (latency or route-specific errors)
- Trigger: Single region P95 latency > 750ms OR API error rate > 1% for targeted model route.
- Quick path:
  1) Reduce concurrency for affected route: POST /admin/routes/<route>/concurrency {"max": 4}.
  2) Switch route to cheaper but faster variant model (model-pin fallback): model:v1-quantized -> model:v1-8bit-fp16.
  3) If latency persists, reject long-tail requests with 429 and clear guidance via Retry-After.

Play C — Model quality regression
- Trigger: Eval set regression > 3% or customer reports degradation across prompts.
- Steps:
  1) Isolate traffic to previous stable model version using route pinning.
  2) Run the regression harness: python tools/eval_harness/run_eval.py --suite nightly-quality --model candidate --baseline stable.
  3) Create a postmortem with side-by-side examples and metric deltas, then run a model-onboarding rollback checklist.

Play D — Security-sensitive incidents
- Trigger: confirmed credentials compromise, PII leakage, or suspicious exfiltration patterns.
- Steps:
  1) Immediately isolate affected tenant(s) and revoke API keys for suspected tokens.
  2) Notify Product Security and Legal.
  3) Begin forensic evidence capture: preserve logs, snapshots of serving instances, and network flows.

SLOs, thresholds and quick indicators (operational cheat-sheet):
- Serving availability SLO: 99.95% per region.
- Latency SLO (generate endpoint): P50 < 100ms, P95 < 300ms (hosted), P95 < 750ms (dedicated).
- Error budget policy: If burn rate > 3x for 30m -> SRE page. If burn rate > 5x for 15m -> declare incident.
- Quick indicators to check first: Redis KVS queue length, GPU utilization % (nvidia-smi), KV cache miss rate, router queue latency.

Operator Skill Ladder (competency milestones and expected behaviors)
- Novice (0–3 months on-call)
  - Can acknowledge incidents and follow a Play B or C with a mentor.
  - Proficient with bridge tooling and status page updates.
  - Knows how to gather key logs and create a clean incident timeline.
- Practitioner (3–12 months)
  - Leads Play B incidents end-to-end.
  - Can run targeted rollbacks and suggest mitigations (e.g., model pinning, concurrency caps).
  - Completes at least 2 game-day exercises per quarter and documents learnings.
- Senior Operator (>12 months)
  - Leads Play A incidents and coordinates cross-team work.
  - Coaches novices, owns one bridge rotation per quarter, performs blameless postmortems and drives remediation.
  - Can author and update runbooks and propose infra changes to reduce toil.

Skill assessment matrix (short checklist used by mentors):
- Can create bridge and assign roles: Y/N
- Can read and interpret P95 latency and error rate dashboards: Y/N
- Can execute safe rollback steps without breaking routing: Y/N
- Can author a customer-facing status message: Y/N

Game-day curriculum (quarterly progression)
- Module 1: Bridge basics and comms (walk-through + 1-hour drill).
- Module 2: Containment plays (rate-limiting, route pinning, model fallback).
- Module 3: Multi-region failover (simulation of region down, full Play A).
- Module 4: Forensics and evidence (capture, retention, and handoff to security).
- Module 5: Postmortem facilitation and action-tracking.

Each game-day includes: playbook run, timed metrics capture (TTI, TTR, MTTR), and a 45-minute retro with a learning card logged to the incident-learning index.

Runbook templates (use copy-and-paste sections)
- Title: <short name>
- Trigger: <alerts or signals>
- Impact: <who is affected>
- Ownership: <team / rotation contact>
- Step 0 (Immediate): acknowledge, initial status, assign bridge roles
- Diagnostics: <commands and dashboards>
- Containment options (ordered): <step-by-step>
- Restoration plan: <canary steps, metrics to watch>
- Communication plan: <customer / internal>
- Post-incident checklist: evidence collection, RCA owner, action items

Appendix: sample commands and dashboard queries
- Check GPU usage: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
- Tail serving logs: sudo journalctl -u rwd-serving -f --lines=500
- Kubernetes control plane: kubectl get pods -n redwood-control -o wide
- Query metrics (Prometheus): rate(http_requests_total{job="router",status=~"5.."}[5m])

Customer status message templates (short, modular fragments)
- Initial (first 10m):
  - Subject: "Service disruption impacting Redwood inference — investigating"
  - Body: "We are investigating an issue affecting inference for some customers. We have an active incident and will share updates every 15 minutes. Impact: some requests may experience errors or increased latency. No confirmations of data exposure at this time."
- Mid-incident update (30–60m):
  - Body: "Mitigation in progress. Traffic has been routed to fallback region for affected customers. We are monitoring P95 latency and error rate; next update in 30 minutes."
- Resolution:
  - Body: "Service restored. Root cause under investigation. We are rolling out post-incident notes and an RCA in 48 hours. If you continue to see issues, please contact support@redwood.ai."

Postmortem taxonomy and evidence checklist
- Type of postmortem: blameless RCA (customer visible) vs internal technical RCA (security-sensitive).
- Evidence to collect within first 24h:
  - Timeline of events with UTC timestamps and actor names.
  - Snapshots of metrics dashboards at 1m, 5m, 15m intervals.
  - Copies of bridge chat/logs and any config changes (terraform plan/apply, API calls).
  - Logs and preserved instance snapshots for forensic teams.
- RCA structure to use:
  1) Summary and impact metrics, 2) Timeline, 3) Contributing factors, 4) Remediation and action owners with deadlines, 5) Customer communication timeline.

Incident learning and action tracking
- All action items must be logged in the incident board with: owner, due date, priority, and verification steps.
- Verification step required before closing: production metrics show no regression for 7 days (SLO verification window).

Mentoring and on-call succession plan
- Shadowing: novices must shadow two full incidents as an observer and one as a deputy before solo shifts.
- Pairing: practitioner-level operators should pair with a senior for first Play A leadership.
- Knowledge checks: after each quarter, operators take a 20-question practical quiz; passing is required to remain on rotation.

Governance and runbook maintenance
- Runbooks are reviewed every 6 months by the owning team or after any incident that exercised the runbook.
- Ownership change requires a short handover doc and reviewers sign-off.

Appendix: Example Slack bridge messages (templates)
- Bridge open (first message):
  "BRIDGE OPEN — Incident RED-2026-123 
  Role assignments: Lead: @alice, System: @bob, Comm: @carol, Liaison: @dave. Initial impact: elevated 5xx for inference-hosted across us-west. Next update in 15m."
- Bridge update:
  "UPDATE +25m — Containment action: traffic routed to fallback-ww-1. P95 latency improved from 680ms to 230ms for canary traffic. Next update in 30m."

Appendix: Contact list (rotation aliases)
- Bridge Lead alias: oncall-bridge@redwood.ai
- SRE Pager alias: sre-pager@redwood.ai
- Customer Liaison: csr-ops@redwood.ai

Document maintenance and feedback
- Maintainer: Aisha Kapoor (oncall-and-incident-response).
- To propose edits: add comments on this page and ping the reviewer list. Significant changes require a game-day validation run.

This page is intentionally focused on operational decision-making and developing on-call competence. For deep-dive technical runbooks, consult the per-service runbook directory linked in Related Pages."
